newsitem.title: UK: BT Shipping second quarter profits rise.
newsitem.headline: BT Shipping second quarter profits rise.

text.p: BT Shipping Ltd said it remains confident of further progress after reporting an increase in second quarter profits.
And it has confirmed it has acquired its first tanker since 1990.
The Bermuda-based tanker owner reported net profit in the three months to the end of June of $1.08 million against $0.45 million in the same period a year earlier.
Net operating revenues stood at $6.98 million, up from $6.44 million.
Chairman and chief executive Eddie Pollock said that spot freight markets had improved during the second quarter as a result of increased oil export activity from the Caribbean.

Three of its vessels had been employed on time charter during the period while the other three had operated mainly on the spot market, primarily in the Caribbean, North and South American trades, Pollock said in a statement.
Chief financial officer Allan Jones said the firm remained confident of further progress due to the improved tanker markets.
"The long term trend is still looking quite healthy," Jones said. However, he cautioned that the start of the third quarter is traditionally slow due to refinery maintenance programmes.
BT Shipping owns and operates a fleet of six 69,900 dwt product carriers acquired from Maersk in 1989 with revenues from its flotation that year on Nasdaq.
BT Shipping confirmed it has acquired the 88,000 dwt crude tanker BT Stream from its largest shareholder, Norwegian shipping group Loki ASA.
BT Shipping declined to comment on market reports the ship cost $13.5 million.
"We had been managing the vessel since last October, and are very happy with it. The 1980-built ship has just been through an extensive dry-docking as is in very good condition," Jones said.
The vessel currently operates in the UK/North Sea/Continent crude oil trade.
It its the first vessel the firm has bought since it acquired a VLCC in 1990 which it subsequently resold.
Loki controls just under 43 percent of BT Shipping, Jones said.
